html:
SMTO-PRL-0003 — That step belongs to a different task

GUID: d2432f99-ebbc-4c19-8c61-2671d4634896
Slug: activity-wrong-owner
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • This task can show you a step that another task started, but only the task that started it can stop it or answer it. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the earlier task in the conversation where this step first appeared, and open that task's Activities section. The step's controls only work from the task that started it.
  2. Use Stop, Provide input or Review approval on the step there. That task is the one allowed to control the step.
  3. If you can't find the earlier task, reload the page and scroll further up the conversation. The task that started the step may be well above the current one.

What success looks like

  • The control works from the original task and the step's status updates.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to control the step from a different task.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An activity control was rejected because the selected activity's run_id differs from the run receiving the request; inherited activities are observation-only in this run.

What this means

  • The selected background activity carries a run_id different from the run receiving the control request. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • The selected background activity carries a run_id different from the run receiving the control request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the observed activity's owner with the current run before issuing any control.

How to fix it

  • Send the stop or input control to the activity's owning run (its run_id and request_id), not to the run that inherited the observation. Do not move execution authority between runs.
  • Open the activity’s owning run and use its current controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported controls are used only from the activity's actual owning run.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
